title: Saṅkalpa (evening)

words.gram: compound; final member dvāra, n., instr. sg. used adverbially
words.meaning: by way of the destruction of all the faults incurred
words.role: states the means: the rite works by removing faults

words.gram: compound ending in -artham (acc. sg. used adverbially, ‘for the sake of’)
words.meaning: for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord
words.role: states the purpose of the act

words.meaning: the sandhyā, the rite of the junction (of night and day)
I shall worship, I shall perform the worship of

samasa.vigraha: उपात्तानां समस्तानां दुरितानां क्षयः, तेन द्वारेण
samasa.meaning: by way of the destruction of all the faults that have been incurred
for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord

translation.literal: By way of the destruction of all the faults incurred by me, for the pleasure of the glorious Supreme Lord, I shall worship the evening sandhyā.
translation.readable: To remove every fault I have incurred, and for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord, I shall perform the evening Sandhyā.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, for the evening service. It names the means — the removal of all the faults one has incurred — and the purpose, the pleasure of the Supreme Lord, and then the act itself. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.
in_the_rite: Evening service, step sankalpa, after the prāṇāyāma.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.
